correctness.rationale: The completed linear two-stage Radau IIA stability map r(z)=(6+2z)/(6-4z+z²) has Taylor coefficients a_1..a_5=1,1/2,1/6,1/36,-1/108. For any row Markov generator with n≤5, the first nonzero (i,j) power is exactly a positive path-sum at the shortest directed distance d≤n−1≤4; unreachable entries are identically zero, and diagonal entries tend to one. Thus every fixed such generator has a (not uniform in Q) positive small-step interval. The irreducible directed six-cycle first reaches displacement five at order h⁵, giving -h⁵/108+O(h⁶); longer directed cycles share this local sign failure. A direct rational-inverse computation for P⁶=I verifies the common positive denominator, four strictly positive offdiagonal numerators, the positive diagonal via Bernstein and shifted certificates, and N_5=h⁵(h⁵+15h⁴+60h³+90h²+36h−12). The latter polynomial has strictly positive derivative on h≥0 and a unique positive root τ≈0.208608859735, so six-cycle entrywise positivity holds exactly for h=0 or h≥τ; the h=1/10 negative witness is -743849/19268401151106. Exact rational checks independently reconstructed every 2..6-cycle class; irreducible cycle diagonalization yields eventual positivity for n≥6. These calculations prove only the explicit finite rational identities, not the general generator theorem, which follows from the shortest-path argument.

value.rationale: The smallest Markov state space permitting loss of end-step positivity at arbitrarily small positive steps is a natural dimension threshold for high-order time integration; an exact six-cycle return interval is a meaningful quantitative complement to generic SSP obstructions. The result is not merely a negative example: it supplies an all-generator five-state guarantee and a sharp classification for the six-state witness, clarifying what step-size reduction can and cannot fix.
